issues.description: Email field is not sanitized before storage, creating XSS vulnerability. An attacker could inject malicious scripts through the email field which would bypass validation.
Email regex is overly permissive and allows invalid emails with dangerous characters like "><script>alert(1)</script>"@x.y
issues.suggestion: Use more robust email validation regex: /^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*$/ or use validator.js library

issues.description: Missing error handling for saveUser() database operation. Database operations can fail for many reasons causing application crashes or inconsistent state.
issues.suggestion: Wrap saveUser() in try-catch block and throw descriptive error: try { await saveUser(user); } catch (error) { throw new Error(`Failed to create user: ${error.message}`); }

issues.description: Sanitization function only escapes basic HTML characters but doesn't handle other XSS vectors like JavaScript events or CSS injection. Missing forward slash escaping for </script> breaks.
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive escaping including '&' (must be first), '/' for script breaks, or use well-tested library like DOMPurify

issues.description: ID generation using Date.now() and Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and has collision risks in high-concurrency scenarios. Math.random() is predictable.
issues.suggestion: Use cryptographically secure ID generation: import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; function generateId(): string { return `user_${randomUUID()}`; }

issues.description: Email and name inputs are not trimmed, allowing leading/trailing whitespace to pass validation, potentially creating duplicate accounts.
issues.suggestion: Trim inputs before validation: const email = input.email?.trim() || ''; const name = input.name?.trim() || '';

issues.description: No maximum length validation on email or name fields, allowing denial-of-service attacks or database errors with extremely long strings.
issues.suggestion: Add length validation: if (email.length > 254) throw new Error('Email too long'); if (name.length > 100) throw new Error('Name too long');

issues.description: Generic error messages could be improved with custom error classes for better error handling and to prevent information leakage.
issues.suggestion: Create custom error class: class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public field?: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; } }

issues.description: Email is lowercased after validation, not before. If validation is case-sensitive, this inconsistency could lead to edge case bugs.
issues.suggestion: Normalize email before validation: const email = input.email?.trim().toLowerCase() || '';

issues.description: Code checks for falsy values but doesn't explicitly handle null/undefined inputs which could cause runtime errors.
issues.suggestion: Use optional chaining: const email = input.email?.trim().toLowerCase(); const name = input.name?.trim();

issues.description: Functions have JSDoc comments but don't document parameters and return values, making it harder for developers to understand function contracts.
issues.suggestion: Add complete JSDoc: @param email - The email address to validate; @returns True if email is valid, false otherwise

issues.description: User properties could be marked readonly to prevent accidental mutation after creation.
issues.suggestion: Use readonly modifiers: readonly id: string; readonly email: string; readonly name: string; readonly createdAt: Date;

codeQuality.summary: Code demonstrates good security awareness with input sanitization and parameterized queries, but contains critical vulnerabilities including unsanitized email field (XSS risk), weak email validation regex, missing error handling for database operations, incomplete sanitization function, and weak ID generation with collision risks. The code requires significant hardening before production use.

recommendations.description: Email field is not sanitized before storage, allowing XSS attacks. An attacker could inject malicious scripts through email (e.g., '<script>alert(1)</script>'@example.com) that bypass validation. IMMEDIATE FIX REQUIRED: Apply sanitizeInput() to email field before creating user object.

Missing error handling for saveUser() database operation. If database fails, application will crash or enter inconsistent state. REQUIRED: Wrap saveUser() in try-catch block and throw descriptive UserCreationError with original error as cause.

Email regex is overly permissive and allows dangerous characters like angle brackets and quotes, enabling potential XSS bypass. RECOMMENDED: Use RFC 5322 compliant regex or well-tested library like validator.js for production-grade email validation.

ID generation using Date.now() and Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and has collision risks in high-concurrency scenarios. Math.random() is predictable. RECOMMENDED: Replace with crypto.randomUUID() for guaranteed uniqueness and cryptographic security.

Sanitization function only escapes basic HTML characters but misses forward slash (for </script> breaks) and ampersand. Missing coverage for JavaScript events and CSS injection vectors. RECOMMENDED: Add comprehensive escaping or use battle-tested library like DOMPurify.

Database dependency is hard-coded with commented-out implementation, making code untestable and violating SOLID principles. RECOMMENDED: Introduce UserRepository interface with DatabaseUserRepository implementation to enable mocking in tests and support future database changes.

No maximum length validation on email/name fields allows denial-of-service attacks with extremely long strings (megabytes) causing memory exhaustion or database errors. RECOMMENDED: Add length limits (254 chars for email per RFC 5321, 100 chars for name).

Email and name inputs are not trimmed before validation, allowing whitespace-padded duplicates (' user@example.com ' vs 'user@example.com'). Also, email is lowercased after validation creating inconsistency. RECOMMENDED: Trim and normalize inputs before validation to prevent duplicate accounts.

Generic Error objects make it difficult for callers to handle errors programmatically and reduce type safety. RECOMMENDED: Create ValidationError and UserCreationError classes with field information for better error handling and debugging.
